newsitem.title: USA: High court tax ruling disappoints natgas producers.
newsitem.headline: High court tax ruling disappoints natgas producers.

text.p: Natural gas producers were disappointed Tuesday with a decision by the U.S. Supreme Court allowing Ohio to tax natural gas marketers and producers from outside the state differently from local gas utilities.
But producers are unlikely to press Congress to address their concern, a spokeswoman for the Natural Gas Supply Association (NGSA) said.
The high court Tuesday upheld a sales tax imposed by the state of Ohio on natural gas sold by marketers and producers from outside the state, but not imposed on gas sold by local utilities.
"This decision does not further the development of a national, competitive marketplace for natural gas," said NGSA president Nicholas Bush.
In a brief to the court in the case pitting General Motors Corp against Ohio, NGSA last year said Ohio's tax violated the Constitution by discriminating against interstate trade.

The tax did not reflect changes in the natural gas market over the last 10 years which had allowed marketers and producers to compete directly with utilities for sales to big customers like GM, producers said.

But the Supreme Court agreed with the state that utilities should be treated differently because, unlike marketers, they had an obligation to provide service to all homes and had to pay a gross receipts tax.
NGSA spokeswoman Charlotte LeGates said Tuesday the group saw little recourse in Congress to address the interstate trade issue.
"The political climate is against federal solutions," she said.
